gate.name: Architecture Gate (G4)

phases.objective: Define the system architecture that satisfies the requirements. Decompose the product into subsystems (structure, actuation, sensing, compute, power), define their interfaces, and allocate budgets (mass, power, compute, cost) across them. Select the actuator class, sensor suite, compute platform, and power source with rationale, checking each against its budget. Record the architecture and the selection decisions into the twin. Whenever you quantify a subsystem-level requirement derived from a system-level one (e.g. this subsystem's mass/power allocation), record it with `twin.record_constraint_set` and set `parent_refs` to the system-level requirement it implements, so the chain from intent down to this allocation stays traceable.

criteria: Trade study performed (alternatives considered and recorded)
gate.name: Concept Selection Gate (G5)

phases.objective: Run a trade study for the product concept, now that its system architecture is decided. Propose 2-3 distinct concepts/approaches that could satisfy that architecture (different actuation mechanisms, structural topologies, or component-level approaches -- whichever varies meaningfully for this product), select the one that best satisfies the requirements, and record the decision with the alternatives considered and why each was rejected (the record-decision tool's `alternatives` field), linked back to the architecture decision via `parent_refs`.

gate.name: Industrial design review

phases.objective: Decide the product's form factor, check that people can use it, and choose finishes that suit how its parts are made, before mechanical design draws the housing. (1) Form factor: list the contents the product must hold (from the architecture and the selected concept: boards, batteries, actuators, bought parts), each with its size and how it is known, and run form_factor_envelope with the internal clearance and the wall thickness (the chosen process's minimum wall, from library.process_limits or library.machine_limits, when a process is chosen), checked against the maximum envelope the requirements state. Record the resulting envelope with twin.record_constraint_set, parent_refs set to the requirement it serves, so mechanical design works to it. (2) Ergonomics: if people hold, press, reach or lift the product, take the intended users from the requirements (ask the person if no requirement says), find a sourced limit for each human-contact feature (an anthropometric dataset or ergonomics guidance, cited with its table and percentile) and run check_ergonomics. If nobody handles it, record that, with the reason, instead. Never supply a body measurement from memory. (3) Colour, material and finish: the look is the person's choice; ask for it if it was not stated. Choose a library appearance per visible part (library.list_appearances; a new one is registered with library.register_appearance, held for the person's approval, with its colour code and a sourced screen value), and run check_cmf_compatibility against each part's material. (4) Joint and edge language: decide how joints show (hidden, flush or expressed, and with which fixings) and how edges are treated (radius or chamfer and where), from the selected concept and the process limits, and record them with twin.record_constraint_set so mechanical design works to them. Record one decision with twin.record_decision covering the envelope, the ergonomics verdict and the finishes, naming every unknown and every assumed value, with its industrial_design field: joint_language, edge_treatment, ergonomics (verdict and the source of the limits, or the reason nobody handles it), finishes (part, appearance, and whether check_cmf_compatibility passed) and open_decisions. Settle each open decision with the person before the gate; the gate is not ready while any remain open.

phases.title: Kickoff
phases.objective: Set the design direction before anything else, in a few minutes. (1) Deciding questions: name the few questions whose answers change this design most (who uses it, the load it carries, the budget, the quantity, the process available, the style), at most eight. Answer each from the goal and the flow context first (source stated); ask the person only what those leave open (source person); where nobody can answer, state your assumption (source assumed) or leave it open (source open). Later phases are briefed with these answers and must not ask them again. (2) Earlier runs: read the lessons from earlier runs on this project in this brief (gate rejections, reviewer findings, recorded lessons) and keep the ones that bear on this design. (3) Directions: name two or three distinct directions for this product type (for a chair: four-leg dowelled, slot-together flat-pack, cantilever), each with a one-line rationale and its main risk, fitting the answers. (4) The pick: if the person picked a direction, record it; if they said "you choose", or nobody can answer yet, record picked 'auto' with the direction you chose and why. Record one decision with twin.record_decision whose kickoff field holds questions [{id, question, answer, source}], directions [{name, rationale, risk}], picked, chosen and why (for auto), and lessons [{text, source_run}]. The gate shows the directions: approving accepts the pick; a retry naming another direction records that one instead. Author no requirements, sketches or CAD here.

criteria: The deciding questions answered, each with its source, none to be asked again

phases.title: Manufacturing Route & Process Selection
phases.objective: Before any detailed design, choose how the part will be made, from what is available. Read the manufacturing context in this brief (route, machines, stock, quantity, budget); ask the person for anything missing rather than assume it. Pick 2 to 4 candidate processes the route allows, source each one's capability limits and costs as design values with their sources, and rank them with the rank_manufacturing_processes skill. Record a decision (record-decision tool) scoped to the project with manufacturing_route (the recommended route 'in_house' or 'vendor', process and material_class) and process_ranking (the candidates with their reasons); a process the person already stated is a one-candidate ranking. Record the chosen process's limits as a constraint set so the design is held to them. If the person cannot decide yet, pass manufacturing_route with deferred: true and their reason. The gate shows the ranking: approving accepts the recommendation; a retry naming another process records that one instead. A decision without manufacturing_route, or a chosen route without process_ranking, leaves the gate not ready.

gate.name: Manufacturing route and process decision
criteria: Candidate processes compared on fit, availability and cost at quantity
Chosen process and material recorded, with its limits as constraints

phases.title: Concept Design
phases.objective: Before any CAD, decide what to build and show it. Work from this brief: the direction picked at kickoff and its answers (one concept develops that direction; a concept that departs from it says why), the requirements and load cases, the chosen manufacturing route, the library's process, machine and material limits (library.process_limits, library.machine_limits, library.get_material), the standard parts and components that can join it (library.standard_part, component.search_intent), and the findings and lessons of earlier runs on this project. Propose 2 or 3 concepts that differ in structure or joinery, each one fit for the route. For each concept draw a labelled sketch with twin.commit_design_sketch as self-contained SVG: front, side and isometric views of a simple block layout of its parts, with part names, joint types, and the key sizes taken from the requirements. Mark every label as intended, assumption or open (an unresolved question); a sketch shows intent and never claims a measured, verified or manufacturable result. Choose one concept and record a decision with twin.record_decision: the selected assembly in its assembly field (every part with its source, made, bought or standard, and every connection between parts with its joint type), concept_options naming each concept with exactly one selected, the alternatives and why each was rejected, parent_refs to the requirements it serves. Record the standard or bought parts the joints rely on (dowels, screws, inserts) with twin.record_component_selection and selection candidate, with their sizes and sources, for the design phase to confirm. Do not author CAD in this phase.

gate.name: Concept Design Gate (G5)
criteria: Two or three concepts proposed, each with a labelled sketch
Selected assembly recorded with every part, connection and joint type
Joints rely on named standard or bought parts with their sources
Concept fits the chosen manufacturing route and its limits
Alternatives recorded with why each was rejected
Sketches labelled as intent; no verified or manufacturable claims

phases.title: Mechanical Design
phases.objective: Design the part THE GOAL DESCRIBES — not a generic or example part. Build the assembly selected at the concept gate: read the concept decision (its assembly lists every part, whether it is made, bought or standard, and every connection with its joint), author one CAD part for each made part, named as in the concept, and join them as decided with the standard parts named there. If the design must depart from the concept, say why and record a revised concept decision with its assembly; the gate checks the committed parts against the latest one. Author the geometry with the FreeCAD tools, sized to the requirements; name each part after what it actually is; use the process and material chosen at the route gate and design to that process's limits (the constraint set recorded there); then PERSIST it with the commit-geometry tool so it becomes a viewable cad_model (a described-but-uncommitted model does NOT count). Record the design rationale: the dimensions, the material, and how the section carries the load. If sizing this part derives a specific numeric spec (e.g. a section dimension driven by the load case), record it with `twin.record_constraint_set` and set `parent_refs` to the system requirement it implements.

gate.name: Mechanical design review (G6)
criteria: The committed geometry is the part the goal asked for
Every part the selected concept makes is committed, joined as the concept decided
Sized to the requirements; material chosen with rationale

phases.title: DFM Review & Manufacturing Plan
phases.objective: Check the committed design against the process chosen at the route gate, with the check_manufacturability skill: each feature (wall thickness, holes, inside corner and bend radii, draft, overhang, envelope) against that process's sourced limits, pass, fail or unknown, saying for each value whether it was measured, declared when the part was authored, or stated. Record failing and unknown findings as evidence against the cad_model. Write the manufacturing plan: stock to buy, operations in order, quantity, and a unit cost only if every input is sourced. Record a decision (record-decision tool) scoped to the project with dfm_review (process, verdict, findings, unknowns, plan). A not_manufacturable verdict leaves the gate not ready: rework the design. An incomplete verdict passes with what could not be checked named; approving accepts it.

gate.name: DFM review (manufacturability)
criteria: Design checked feature by feature against the chosen process
Each value's basis stated (measured, declared or stated)
Manufacturing plan with stock and operations in order

phases.title: Simulation & V&V
phases.objective: Validate the part against its safety-factor requirement. Mesh the committed geometry and run CalculiX FEA under the load case; extract the max stress and safety factor; record a pass/fail verdict against the requirement. If FEA tooling is unavailable, say so explicitly — do NOT present a hand-calc as FEA.

gate.name: V&V sign-off (G7)
criteria: FEA executed on the committed geometry
Pass/fail verdict recorded against the requirement
